clue.text: Majority is cut in Bosnia

indicators.note: something cut loses its tail, so the final letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: majority as a plural subject: 'most are' takes the plural verb where 'majority is' takes the singular

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the governing majority has been reduced in Bosnia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Majority is' becomes MOST ARE (the plural form of the same statement), and 'cut' docks its last letter E. The definition follows the puzzle's pattern of naming a place by where it lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Mostar is a city in Bosnia and Herzegovina, famous for its old bridge, so 'in Bosnia' places it.

clue.text: Leader of misquotation in 20

parts.note: Shakespeare wrote 'Lay on', but the line is popularly misquoted as 'Lead on', making this thane the leader in the misquoted version

explanation.surface: A puzzle about who leads in a misremembered line from the play.
explanation.walkthrough: In the play's last scene the tyrant says 'Lay on, ...'; the familiar misquotation 'Lead on, ...' casts the addressee as a leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The thane addressed in the famous misquoted line 'Lead on' is a character in the Scottish play.

clue.text: Grass, usually down the map

definitions.meaning: turf or a stretch of grassy ground
the abbreviation of southward, the direction a map conventionally places at the bottom

explanation.surface: A note that the lawn generally lies towards the bottom of the plan.
explanation.walkthrough: S'WARD is a written abbreviation of 'southward'; 'usually' covers the fact that maps conventionally have south at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A sward is an expanse of short grass, a literary word for turf.

clue.text: I can get in trouble for being stimulating

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they might be punished for being provocative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' looks like one phrase, but 'in' belongs to the fodder: ICANGETIN, stirred by 'trouble', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An antigenic substance stimulates the immune system to produce antibodies, so it is stimulating in a biological sense.

clue.text: Lustreless chalice keeping hot to form a pair

parts.note: a matt or mat finish has no shine

indicators.note: the cup keeps the next letter inside it, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a chalice is a cup, especially a ceremonial one
H is the usual abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A dull goblet with something hot inside is matched to make a set.
explanation.definitionFit: To match up is to pair things off together, an idiomatic phrasal verb.

clue.text: Military award includes booze out of house in 20

indicators.note: the medal letters include another piece placed between them

parts.note: MM is the Military Medal

indicators.note: the house letters are taken out of the booze

parts.note: booze is alcohol

explanation.surface: A soldier's decoration somehow involves drinking outside the home in the play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Military award' is not the more familiar MC here but the Military Medal; 'house' is lost from the drink, not from the soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Malcolm, Duncan's elder son, is a character in the Scottish play who becomes king at the end.

clue.text: Apocryphal portion to lead

indicators.note: to lead is to go in front, so the word to comes before the other piece

parts.note: taken as written
a bit is a portion or piece

explanation.surface: Part of a dubious story is set to take the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobit is a book of the Apocrypha, so the adjective stands for it as a crossword shorthand for an apocryphal book.

clue.text: Toiletry article hard to treat as nonexistent

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
to airbrush something out of a photo or a record is to act as if it never existed

explanation.surface: Something in the bathroom is difficult to pretend away.
explanation.definitionFit: A brush for the hair is an item kept on the dressing table among one's toiletries.

clue.text: Drink in 20

definitions.meaning: a dark brown beer brewed from charred malt
the drunken gatekeeper of the knocking scene in the Scottish play

explanation.definitionFit: Porter is a dark beer, and the Porter is the comic gatekeeper in the Scottish play's knocking scene.

clue.text: Tom gets drug from goddess in 20

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A tomcat picks up something illicit from a deity in the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Hecate, Greek goddess of witchcraft, appears in the Scottish play as mistress of the witches.

clue.text: Make a good map of premier home

parts.note: to chart is to map
well, as in 'all is well', means good

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to do some decent cartography at the prime minister's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a good map' read as an instruction means 'chart well'; 'Make a' only frames the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartwell in Kent was the country house of Winston Churchill, a British prime minister or premier.

clue.text: Rose, the British Queen

parts.note: I is Italian for 'the' (masculine plural)
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A flower named after the monarch of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'the' is foreign: Italian I, the plural definite article.
explanation.definitionFit: The brier or briar rose is a wild rose, the sweetbrier or dog rose.

clue.text: A Frenchwoman's breast is like virgin soil

parts.note: the French for 'a' is UN, the indefinite article
a dug is an udder or teat, an old word for a breast

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman's bosom compared to untouched earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The French word for 'a' gives UN; strictly a woman would be 'une', but the surface's lady only signals the language.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgin soil has never been dug, so it is undug: not yet turned by spade or plough.

clue.text: Commercial work on board is such as may be undertaken

indicators.note: one piece sits on the other, so it comes first in the across answer

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, an AD
OP is short for opus, a work
a board is a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: An advert for a project carried out on deck could be taken on.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adoptable can be taken on or undertaken, as a cause or a child may be.

clue.text: Mbeki's lot in escape from 20

indicators.note: the party is placed in the verb for escaping

parts.note: to flee is to escape
Thabo Mbeki led the ANC, the African National Congress

explanation.surface: The South African president's party is on the run from the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleance, Banquo's son, escapes the murderers in the Scottish play.

clue.text: From Eminem music I'm missing movement for reconciliation

indicators.note: the answer is made out of these letters, rearranged, once some are set aside

parts.note: taken as written; 'missing' says these letters are left out

explanation.surface: A rapper's tunes, minus the singer, become a church unity drive.
explanation.walkthrough: Take EMINEM MUSIC, remove I and M ('I'm missing'), and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecumenism is the movement seeking unity and reconciliation among the Christian churches.

clue.text: Average, like a 23 in 20

definitions.meaning: middling, in the middle of a scale
someone who communicates with spirits, as the play's weird sisters do

explanation.surface: Ordinary, like one of the weird sisters in the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Medium means average in size, and a medium is a spiritualist like the play's witches.

clue.text: Put on vestment, one in 20

parts.note: to don is to put on clothing
an alb is a white priestly vestment
A means one

explanation.surface: A churchman robes himself, as one character in the play.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is wordplay and, loosely, definition: the name is built from DON, ALB, A and IN, and it belongs to one of the people in the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Donalbain, Duncan's younger son, is a character in the Scottish play.

clue.text: One who seeks payment has power in 20

parts.note: a dun is a creditor pressing for payment
can means is able to, has the power

explanation.surface: A debt collector holds sway in the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Duncan is the king of Scotland murdered in the Scottish play.

clue.text: Retribution seems in order

indicators.note: put in a new order, these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting one's comeuppance appears fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is 'order' alone, so 'in' joins 'seems' as fodder: SEEMSIN rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis, from the Greek goddess of retribution, means a just punishment or downfall.

clue.text: Utilitarian tendency for bad actor

parts.note: a bent is a natural inclination
a ham is an over-the-top performer

explanation.surface: A practical inclination suits a poor performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Bentham founded utilitarianism, so he is the archetypal utilitarian.

clue.text: Put a stop to quoting part of 20

parts.note: to ban is to put a stop to

indicators.note: only a part of the following word is used, its opening letters

explanation.surface: Someone stops quoting a section of the play.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition follows the puzzle's pattern, 'of 20' meaning a character of the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Banquo is the general murdered by order of the king in the Scottish play, whose ghost then appears.

clue.text: American subject holds award for play

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: mathematics is called math in America
CBE is Commander of the Order of the British Empire, an honour

explanation.surface: A US school subject wins an honour for a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish play by Shakespeare, the tragedy all the other themed clues refer to.

clue.text: Say a business? Say yes

indicators.note: say introduces the spoken version of the following words

parts.note: a firm is a business

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to call it a company, and agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: To affirm is to state positively, to assent.

clue.text: She's locally privileged to provide for a new me

indicators.note: the letters are to be made to provide something new, rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman with civic rights is asked to supply a fresh identity.
explanation.walkthrough: FORANEWME is rearranged. 'Locally' refers to the rights a freewoman holds in her own town.
explanation.definitionFit: A freewoman holds the freedom of a city or borough, with privileges in that locality.

clue.text: One of three which can be heard in 20

indicators.note: the word is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: these words are said aloud, and what is heard is the sound this part of the answer needs

explanation.surface: One of a trio who can be heard in the play.
explanation.definitionFit: The play opens with three weird sisters, so a witch is one of three in it.

clue.text: Only rich people have the words

indicators.note: the words 'have' the answer contained in them

explanation.surface: Only wealthy people possess the text.
explanation.definitionFit: The lyric, or lyrics, of a song are its words.

clue.text: Three of three eat up money

indicators.note: the letters eat, so take in, the next piece
only three of the word's five letters are used, its last three

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A trio of a trio finish their meal, and money changes hands.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency of India, Pakistan and other countries.

clue.text: Dot what should be dotted, silly fool

indicators.note: silly letters are mixed up

parts.note: the i's are what one dots, as in 'dot the i's and cross the t's'

explanation.surface: An instruction to dot properly, followed by an insult.
explanation.walkthrough: One dots the i's (and crosses the t's), so two I's join DOT before 'silly' rearranges.

clue.text: Crab (for hanging Jeff Davis) could be popular in the Home Counties

indicators.note: these letters could be rearranged into something else

parts.note: the Home Counties lie around London in the South East, SE

explanation.surface: A crab apple, of the tree for hanging a Confederate leader, might be liked around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties round London. The bracket recalls the Union song 'We'll hang Jeff Davis from a sour apple tree' (Davis led the Confederacy).

clue.text: Many get stress when lost in Tennessee

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, many

indicators.note: the 'when' word is lost from the stress word

parts.note: emphasis is stress
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

clue.text: Strange men she has to get in her toils

indicators.note: strange letters are oddly arranged

explanation.surface: Peculiar men who are caught up in a woman's schemes.
